newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania constitutional court clears Ukraine treaty.
newsitem.headline: Romania constitutional court clears Ukraine treaty.

text.p: Romania's constitutional court on Friday dismissed a challenge by Supreme Court judges against a key treaty with post-Soviet Ukraine, state news agency Rompres said.

The court ruled that the treaty, which confirms existing borders between the two states and Kiev's authority over lands lost by Romania before World War Two, was in line with the post-communist constitution of 1991.
The Ukrainian parliament voted on Thursday to ratify the pact, already endorsed by the Romanian parliament.
The treaty, signed by presidents Emil Constantinescu of Romania and Leonid Kuchma of Ukraine on June 2, was praised by U.S. President Bill Clinton, who visited Bucharest last week.

Friday's ruling rejected the challenge by 17 Supreme Court judges on the grounds that it was submitted after Constantinescu signed the treaty into law. The judges had argued that it violated the constitution, which proclaims Romania as a "unitary and indivisible state".

In 1940 the Soviet Union seized southern Bessarabia and northern Bukovina under a pact with Nazi Germany. In 1948 it also gained the tiny but strategically important Serpent Island in the Black Sea. The lands are now part of modern-day Ukraine.
Last year Romania signed a similar pact with Hungary, ending old rifts over borders and minorities.
